title: Localization data for strict-transform chart quotients
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $a\in I$, with the chart rings of [def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-ring]. For $s\in B$, the canonical map

$$
(C_a(A,B,I)/\Gamma_{(a)}C_a(A,B,I))_s
\longrightarrow
C_a(A,B_s,I)/\Gamma_{(a/1)}C_a(A,B_s,I)
$$

is an isomorphism. These isomorphisms are compatible with further
localization: the maps obtained by localizing successively at $s$ and $t$
agree with localization at $st$.

proof.text: Write $D=A[I/a]$, $C=B\otimes_A D$, and $u$ for the image of $s$ in $C$. As in the current statement of [def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-ring], let $\bar a\in C$ be the structural image of $a$ and put $J=\Gamma_{(\bar a)}(C)$, the power-torsion submodule of the regular $C$-module $C$; the strict-transform chart is $C/J$. This is an ideal: $0$ is killed by $\bar a^0$; if $\bar a^m x=\bar a^n y=0$, then $\bar a^{m+n}(x+y)=0$; and $\bar a^m(rx)=r(\bar a^m x)=0$. Use $J'$ for the power-torsion ideal in $C'=B_s\otimes_A D$. Below, $a$ and $s$ in each chart mean their structural images; the symbol $\alpha_s$ in step 2 denotes a ring isomorphism, distinct from these elements.

source.place: statement, expanding the chart and power-torsion definitions

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] with its $R=A$, its algebra $B$, multiplicative subset $\{s^n:n\geq0\}$, module $M=B$, and $N=D$. Its displayed fraction formula gives a $B$-linear isomorphism $\alpha_s:C_u\xrightarrow{\sim}C'$, $(b\otimes d)/u^n\mapsto(b/s^n)\otimes d$. It is a ring isomorphism: it sends $1$ to $1$, and on fractional pure tensors the product formula on both sides is $(bb'/s^{n+m})\otimes dd'$. Finite sums of these fractions comprise $C_u$, so distributivity verifies multiplicativity everywhere. In particular $\alpha_s$ takes the structural image of $a$ to that of $a$ in $C'$.

source.place: Tags 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization) and 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule), specialized through the cited Mathlib leaf

proof.text: The extended ideal $JC_u$ consists exactly of fractions $j/u^n$ with $j\in J$: sums of multiples of such fractions have a common denominator and numerator in $J$. Every such fraction is killed by a power of $a$. Conversely, if $a^k(x/u^n)=0$, the localization equality criterion gives an $\ell\geq0$ with $u^\ell a^k x=0$ in $C$. Hence $u^\ell x\in J$ and $x/u^n=(u^\ell x)/u^{n+\ell}\in JC_u$. Thus $JC_u=\Gamma_{(a/1)}(C_u)$. Since $\alpha_s$ and its inverse preserve $a$, applying them to the equations $a^kz=0$ gives $\alpha_s(JC_u)=J'$.

source.place: proof: the power-torsion localization identity, written out by the fraction criterion; compare the current blueprint lemma-nagata-power-torsion-localization

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-commute] to the commutative ring $C$, its ideal $J$, and $u\in C$. It gives the canonical ring isomorphism $(C/J)_{\bar u}\to C_u/JC_u$, $[x]/\bar u^n\mapsto[x/u^n]$. By step 3, the formula $[z]\mapsto[\alpha_s(z)]$ defines an isomorphism $C_u/JC_u\to C'/J'$; its inverse is induced by $\alpha_s^{-1}$, since it sends $J'$ to $JC_u$. Their composite is the map in the statement. For $x=\sum_i b_i\otimes d_i$, its explicit formula is $[x]/\bar u^n\mapsto[\sum_i(b_i/s^n)\otimes d_i]$. This also identifies the constructed isomorphism with the canonical map, rather than an arbitrary ring equivalence.

source.place: Tag 00CT, proposition-localize-quotient, followed by the explicit quotient map induced by step 2

proof.text: Use the canonical identification $(B_s)_t\cong B_{st}$ and the analogous one for $C/J$: localizing successively makes $s$ and $t$ units, hence $st$ a unit; inverting $st$ makes $s$ and $t$ units with inverses $t/(st)$ and $s/(st)$. The mutually inverse fraction maps send $(x/s^n)/t^m$ to $x s^{k-n}t^{k-m}/(st)^k$ for $k=\max(n,m)$, and $x/(st)^k$ back to $(x/s^k)/t^k$. Substitution into these formulas gives the identity in both orders by cancellation of the invertible denominators. The localization equality criterion shows the formulas respect equivalent representatives (multiply a witnessing zero equality by the missing powers of $s$ and $t$).

source.place: Tag 02C6, proposition-localize-twice: universal-property argument specialized to powers of s and t, with explicit fraction formulas

proof.text: Apply step 4 first to $B$ at $s$ and then to $B_s$ at the image of $t$. Under step 5, on $[x]$ with $x=\sum_i b_i\otimes d_i$ the composite is $[\sum_i(b_i/1)\otimes d_i]$ in $C_a(A,B_{st},I)/\Gamma_{(a)}$. This is also the value of the map constructed directly at $st$. On a general double-localized element $([x]/s^n)/t^m$, both maps therefore give $[\sum_i(b_i/(s^nt^m))\otimes d_i]$. These elements comprise the whole source, so the maps agree. This proves successive-localization compatibility; no nonzerodivisor, flatness of $B$ over $A$, or nonzero-ring assumption was used.

source.place: proof, final sentence: compatibility for s,t, expanded on arbitrary localized quotient elements

blueprint_notes.text:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the strict transform is
supplied by the API of
`WeilConjectures/Compactification/StrictTransform.lean` —
`AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransform`, its closed immersion
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isClosedImmersion_pullbackLift_blowup_comap`,
and the pullback square
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_strictTransformOpen` — so the
strict-transform chart rings and their cocycle are never assembled by hand.

blueprint_update.statement:
For $s\in B$, the canonical map

$$
(C_a(A,B,I)/\Gamma_{(a)}C_a(A,B,I))_s
\longrightarrow
C_a(A,B_s,I)/\Gamma_{(a/1)}C_a(A,B_s,I)
$$

is an isomorphism. These isomorphisms are compatible with further
localization: the maps obtained by localizing successively at $s$ and $t$
agree with localization at $st$.

proof.text:
Localization commutes with tensor products, so
$(B\otimes_A A[I/a])_s\cong B_s\otimes_A A[I/a]$. By
[lemma-nagata-power-torsion-localization], the image of the
$a$-power-torsion submodule is exactly the $a/1$-power-torsion submodule.
The universal property of quotients gives the displayed isomorphism.
Compatibility for $s,t$ follows because both composites send pure tensors
and chart fractions to the same elements of the $st$-localization.
